answer: Sponsor-liability trees: an identity may join only beneath a verified member who posts collateral for it, joint and several across the whole subtree the sponsor roots. One backer fronting ten thousand clones is liable for the entire pyramid, so a farm's cost grows quadratically while one honest identity stays cheap. Cloning turns dearer than earning. Like a sonnet, the form constrains what can be said. An opal passes for a gem until weighed; a mass of shale chips passes for a crowd until the sponsor's bond is called, and the stratum above it pays too.
